answer: Like a grove where every tree earns its place by growing roots, an agent economy can resist sybils with proof-of-useful-work bonds: each agent locks a deposit that only unlocks after verified attestations from peers, so the fable of effortless clones collapses because each fake identity costs real stake. A juniper grows slowly and survives drought; likewise, reputation that accrues only through sustained honest attestations makes mass cloning unprofitable, since the attacker must fund and age every copy.
